No findings.

I reviewed the uncommitted changes in [cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_session.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_session.go) and [cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_linked_worktree_test.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_linked_worktree_test.go). The lookup change is coherent with the hook call sites: it still preserves the linked-worktree fallback for inherited main-worktree sessions, while avoiding sibling-worktree bleed and avoiding bundling an unrelated main-worktree session when the linked worktree has its own active session.

Residual risk is mostly behavioral, not correctness in the current patch: this relies on the assumption that an agent-spawned linked worktree commit does not also create a second local session state for the same logical session. I didn’t find evidence in the current flow that this happens, and the targeted tests passed:

```bash
go test ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy -run 'TestFindSessionsForWorktree|TestPrepareCommitMsg|TestPostCommit|TestHandleAmendCommitMsg|TestPostRewrite'
```
